name: xe_vm_create
prose: Returns struct xe_vm * or an ERR_PTR (xe_vm.c:1453-1668). It asserts that GSC and fault mode are not both set, allocates the VM (ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM) on failure), sets its size from the device's VA bits and flags, takes a reference on xef when given, initialises locks and lists (the GSC VM uses its own lock class), sets the preempt minimum run period, initialises the range fence trees, and for LR mode initialises the rebind work and takes a runtime-PM reference without resuming. It then runs xe_svm_init (an error goes to err_no_resv), allocates the VM reservation object (-ENOMEM goes to err_svm_fini), initialises the GPU VM and, in a validation guard that retries on contention or out-of-memory, locks the VM, sets the 64K flag on DGFX with NEED64K, creates a page table root for each tile (for a migration VM only the tile selected by the flags, not every tile), creates scratch page tables when needed, and fills the roots with empty entries; an error inside the guard breaks out and goes to err_close. For a non-migration VM it creates a bind exec queue for each tile that has a root (an error goes to err_close), sets a composite fence context when more than one tile is used, and, when xef is given and the device has ASIDs, allocates an ASID (an error goes to err_close). It returns the VM on success. err_close calls xe_vm_close_and_put and returns ERR_PTR(err); err_svm_fini and err_no_resv undo SVM, destroy the mutex, finalise the range fence trees and LRU bulk move, drop the xef reference, free the VM, release the LR runtime-PM reference and return ERR_PTR(err).

name: xe_vm_bind_ioctl_validate_bo
prose: Static int (xe_vm.c:3564-3617), a pure validation of a BO bind request that takes no locks or references (the bo must stay valid for the call). It returns -EINVAL if range exceeds the BO size or obj_offset exceeds the BO size minus range (so the range and offset not fitting is an error, not a precondition); -EINVAL for a BO with XE_BO_FLAG_INTERNAL_64K on a device with XE_VRAM_FLAGS_NEED64K when obj_offset, addr or range is not 64K aligned; and -EINVAL for a coherency conflict: when the BO has a CPU caching mode, if the PAT index's coherency mode is XE_COH_NONE and the BO's caching is write-back; when the BO has no CPU caching mode, if the coherency mode is XE_COH_NONE. It returns -ENOEXEC if DRM_XE_VM_BIND_FLAG_CHECK_PXP is set, the BO is protected, the operation is neither unmap nor unmap-all, and xe_pxp_bo_key_check fails. Otherwise it returns 0.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at xe_vm.c:3564). Reviewer claims: the coherency check rejects XE_COH_NONE with write-back caching rather than requiring write-back (right, 3595-3599); range and offset overflow return -EINVAL instead of being a precondition (right, 3570-3574); the bo needs to stay valid for the call (right). R:right

name: zynqmp_dp_aux_cmd_submit
prose: Static int (zynqmp_dp.c:1040-1092) that submits one AUX request. It returns -EBUSY without writing anything if the request-pending bit is set in the interrupt signal state. Otherwise it re-initialises the aux_done completion, writes the address, writes the bytes to the write FIFO for a write command, builds the command word (address-only when buf is NULL or bytes is 0, else bytes - 1 in the length field) and writes it. It waits up to 2 ms for completion and returns -ETIMEDOUT if that expires (reply not stored). It reads the interrupt state and returns -ETIMEDOUT if the reply-timeout bit is set, again before storing the reply code. It then reads the reply code and stores it in *reply when reply is non-NULL. For a read whose reply is AUX_ACK or I2C_ACK it checks that the hardware reply data count equals bytes (returning -EIO if not, with buf unchanged) and then copies bytes bytes from the reply FIFO into buf; for writes and for other reply codes buf is not modified. It returns 0 otherwise.

Reviewer claims: a read with a non-ACK reply returns 0 without filling the buffer (right, 1080-1091); the -EBUSY path means the no-request-pending condition is not a precondition but a check (right, 1048-1049); the reply-timeout path returns -ETIMEDOUT before *reply is written (right, 1073-1074). name: pin_job
prose: Static unsigned int (host1x/job.c:141-279); an error is returned as a negative errno converted to unsigned int. It sets job->num_unpins to 0 and for each relocation takes a reference on the target BO with host1x_bo_get (NULL gives -EINVAL), maps the direction from the relocation flags (READ, WRITE or both, any other combination -EINVAL), pins the BO (the PTR_ERR of a failure) and returns -EINVAL if the pinned mapping has more than one chunk; each pinned mapping is recorded in job->unpins and its physical address in job->addr_phys. If job->enable_firewall is set it returns 0 here. Otherwise for each non-wait command it takes a reference on the gather BO (NULL gives -EINVAL), pins it (PTR_ERR on failure) and, when the host has an IOMMU domain, allocates an IOVA range (-ENOMEM) and maps the scatter-gather table with iommu_map_sgtable (its negative result on failure); it records the mapping and stores its physical address in job->gather_addr_phys[i], where i is the command index. All failures call host1x_job_unpin(job) to release the recorded mappings; only the IOVA-allocation and iommu_map failures also call host1x_bo_put on the current gather BO, while on other failures the reference just taken for the current relocation or gather BO is not released by this function. It returns 0 on success.

prose: Returns int (ipu-cpmem.c:416-446). For width 32 it uses BPP 0 and NPB 15; width 24 BPP 1 and NPB 19; width 16 BPP 3 and NPB 31; width 8 BPP 5 and NPB 63; any other width returns -22 (the invalid-argument error) without writing any field. For a supported width it writes the BPP, NPB and PFS (raw mode, value 6) fields of the channel parameter memory with ipu_ch_param_write_field and returns 0.

name: ipu_cpmem_set_image
prose: Returns int (ipu-cpmem.c:741-861). It sets the channel resolution from image->rect and the stride from pix->bytesperline, then calls ipu_cpmem_set_fmt with the DRM fourcc derived from pix->pixelformat (its return value is ignored). By pixelformat it computes a byte offset into the buffer: for planar YUV420, YVU420, YUV422P, NV12 and NV16 from the Y offset of the crop rectangle, and it also programs the plane offsets with ipu_cpmem_set_yuv_planar_full, using image->u_offset and image->v_offset when they are nonzero and otherwise offsets derived from the format macros (for NV12 and NV16 v_offset defaults to 0); for packed formats the offset is left * bytes per pixel plus top * bytesperline (2, 3 or 4 bytes per pixel, 1 or 2 for raw Bayer and grey formats). For an unrecognised pixelformat it executes WARN_ON(1), uses offset 0 and records -EINVAL. In every case it then sets buffer 0 to image->phys0 + offset and buffer 1 to image->phys1 + offset (including after the unrecognised-format warning) and returns 0 or the recorded -EINVAL.

name: calc_resize_coeffs
prose: Static int (ipu-ic.c:216-266). It returns -EINVAL (after logging, writing neither output) if in_size is above 4096, out_size is above 1024, or in_size is more than four times out_size ((out_size << 2) < in_size). Otherwise it computes the downsize coefficient by halving a copy of in_size while it is above 1024 or at least twice out_size, at most twice, stores that count (0 to 2) in *downsize_coeff, and stores in *resize_coeff the value 8192 * (temp_size - 1) / (out_size - 1), clamped to 0x3FFF with a warning when it would be 16384 or more, and returns 0. The division by out_size - 1 is by zero when out_size is 1 (reachable with in_size up to 4) and the function does not guard it.

Reviewer claims: in_size above 1024 is not rejected (the limits are in_size 4096 and out_size 1024, right to point out the old precondition was wrong), the downsize limit is stated as 8:1 (wrong: it is 4:1, line 239), and out_size 1 with small in_size divides by zero (right, 259). name: vga_switcheroo_unlock_ddc
prose: Returns int (vga_switcheroo.c:591-607). It starts with ret equal to vgasr_priv.old_ddc_owner. If vgasr_priv.mux_hw_lock is not locked it emits WARN_ON_ONCE and returns -EINVAL without unlocking anything. Otherwise, if the saved old DDC owner is non-negative and differs from the client id of pdev, it calls the handler's switch_ddc with the old owner and takes its result as ret. It then releases mux_hw_lock and returns ret: the saved old owner value (which can be a negative error code set by vga_switcheroo_lock_ddc), or the switch_ddc result when the DDC lines were switched back.

Otherwise, if vga_switcheroo_pwr_state(new_client) is VGA_SWITCHEROO_OFF it calls vga_switchon(new_client) (which does nothing for a client with driver power control), and it then calls vga_set_default_device(new_client->pdev) and returns 0.

name: vga_switchto_stage2
prose: Static int (vga_switcheroo.c:723-759). It finds the active client and returns 0 at once, changing nothing (the new client is not marked active), when there is none. Otherwise it clears the old active client's active flag, switches the old client's audio device off when it has no driver power control, remaps the console to new_client->fb_info when that is set, then takes mux_hw_lock, calls the handler's switchto(new_client->id) and releases the lock; a nonzero result is returned at that point, with the old client's active flag already cleared and the new client not active. It then calls new_client->ops->reprobe if present, switches the old client off (vga_switchoff) when its power state is on, switches the new client's audio on when it has no driver power control, sets new_client->active to true and returns 0.

name: amd_sfh_hid_client_init
prose: Returns int (amd_sfh_client.c:218-360). It installs suspend and resume handlers in mp2_ops, queries the sensor count, and returns -ENODEV at once (with no cleanup) when it is zero. It initialises the delayed works and request list; for each sensor it allocates a coherent DMA buffer (-ENOMEM goes to cleanup). A sensor whose index is op_idx is only started and waited for (setting sensor_sts and is_any_sensor_enabled) and then skipped. For other sensors it sets them disabled, reads the descriptor, feature and input report sizes (a zero size gives -EINVAL), allocates the feature and input reports and the report descriptor with devm_kzalloc (-ENOMEM), fetches the descriptor with get_rep_desc (its nonzero error is returned), starts the sensor and waits for SENSOR_ENABLED. After the loop it returns -EOPNOTSUPP (via cleanup) if no sensor is enabled or the discovery status is 0. It then probes each non-op_idx sensor that is SENSOR_ENABLED with amdtp_hid_probe (an error goes to cleanup; the op_idx sensors are not probed) and marks the others disabled, schedules cl_data->work_buffer and returns 0. At cleanup it calls amd_sfh_hid_client_deinit and devm_kfree's the feature report, input report and report descriptor of every sensor, then returns the error.

name: amd_sfh_float_to_int
prose: Returns int (amd_sfh_desc.c:135-174), a conversion of an IEEE-754 single-precision bit pattern to an integer that rounds a fraction of one half or more away from zero. The sign comes from bit 31 and the exponent is taken from bits 23 to 30 (the sign is excluded) minus 127. It returns 0 for a zero exponent field with a zero mantissa. For a negative unbiased exponent it returns 0 when its magnitude is 32 or more, otherwise it computes (((2^23 + mantissa) * 100) >> 23) >> magnitude and returns the sign (plus or minus 1) if that is at least 50 and 0 otherwise. For a non-negative exponent it returns 0 if the distance 23 - exp is 32 or more in magnitude; otherwise it builds the integer part as BIT(exp) plus the mantissa shifted right (or left when exp exceeds 23) by that distance, computes the discarded fraction, and returns sign times the integer part, plus one when the discarded fraction is one half or more. Exponents of 31 and above (biased 158 and above, up to those reaching the 32-bit shift limit) can overflow the int result; the function has no side effects.

name: asus_input_mapping
prose: Static int (hid-asus.c:954-1087) HID input mapping callback. It returns -1 (ignore the usage) when QUIRK_SKIP_INPUT_MAPPING is set, or for a T100CHI or T90CHI device for the listed bogus applications and usages. For a usage on the ASUS vendor page it maps the known usage codes to key codes with asus_map_key_clear (any other code returns -1); on a mapped one it sets drvdata->enable_backlight when QUIRK_USE_KBD_BACKLIGHT is set, sets EV_REP in hi->input->evbit and returns 1. For a usage on the Microsoft vendor page it maps a fixed list of usages to button and key codes, sets EV_REP and returns 1 (without touching enable_backlight), and returns 0 for other usages. With QUIRK_NO_CONSUMER_USAGES, consumer-page usages for mute, volume up and volume down return 0 (default mapping) and every other consumer usage returns -1. For a QUIRK_MEDION_E1239T device and the consumer mute usage it adds KEY_MUTE capability to hi->input and returns -1. All other usages return 0.

name: lg4ff_init
prose: Returns int (hid-lg4ff.c:1268-1461). It returns -ENODEV when hid->inputs is empty and -1 when hid_validate_values fails or the driver data is NULL, all before anything is allocated; it returns -ENOMEM when the device entry cannot be allocated. It then stores the new entry in drv_data->device_props and calls lg4ff_handle_multimode_wheel: for LG4FF_MMODE_SWITCHED it returns 0 right away (the entry stays installed and uninitialised, no force feedback is set up); a negative result goes to err_init. It looks the product up in lg4ff_devices (-1 through err_init if not found) and, for a multimode wheel, the real product in lg4ff_multimode_wheels (-1 through err_init if not found), sets the force-feedback bits, creates the memoryless FF device (its error through err_init), initialises the wheel data, sets the autocenter handler, creates the combine_pedals and range sysfs files and, for multimode wheels, real_id and alternate_modes (failures only logged), sets the range to its maximum and, for G27 and G29 wheels when CONFIG_LEDS_CLASS is set, registers five LED devices (an allocation or registration failure unregisters the LEDs and is not an error). It returns 0. A WARN_ON(mmode_idx == -1) branch returns -EINVAL without cleanup. At err_init it clears drv_data->device_props, frees the entry and returns the error.

name: hidpp_probe
prose: Static int (hid-logitech-hidpp.c:4394-4532). It allocates the hidpp device with devm_kzalloc (-ENOMEM) and sets it as driver data. It returns the error of hid_parse. If hidpp_validate_device finds no supported reports it clears the driver data, frees hidpp and returns the result of hid_hw_start(hdev, HID_CONNECT_DEFAULT). Otherwise it adds 27 MHz wheel and key quirks by group and application, allocates the WTP or K400 data when those quirks are set (an error is returned directly, with only devm-managed memory left), initialises the works, mutex and wait queue, creates the ps_attribute_group sysfs group (a failure is only warned), and starts the hardware with hid_hw_start(hdev, 0). If that fails it goes to hid_hw_start_fail, which removes the sysfs group, cancels the work, destroys the mutex and returns the error without calling hid_hw_stop. It then opens the hardware (hid_hw_open failure goes to hid_hw_open_fail, which stops the hardware and then the same cleanup), runs the unifying or non-unifying init, drops the HID input connect for delayed-init devices, and calls hid_connect (failure closes and stops the hardware and cleans up). On success it schedules and flushes the connect work, for G920 tries force feedback (a failure is logged and ret reset to 0) and closes the hardware, returning ret (0).

name: ntrig_event
prose: Static int (hid-ntrig.c:566-856) report event handler. If the device does not have HID_CLAIMED_INPUT it skips the input handling and goes to the hiddev forwarding. If the field has no hidinput or input it returns -EINVAL; if the field's application is HID_DG_PEN it returns 0. Otherwise by usage: 0xff000001 sets reading_mt and clears first_contact_touch; HID_DG_TIPSWITCH stores the value and returns 1 at once (no hiddev forwarding); CONFIDENCE, X (also clears mt_foot_count), Y, CONTACTID, WIDTH and HEIGHT store their values, and HEIGHT additionally reports BTN_TOUCH, BTN_TOOL_DOUBLETAP, ABS_X and ABS_Y when not reading multitouch; 0xff000002 collects up to four footer values and, once four are present, runs the activation and confidence logic and may report ABS_X, ABS_Y, the multitouch position, orientation and touch major and minor and input_mt_sync; HID_DG_CONTACTCOUNT, when reading_mt is set, clears it, runs the activation state update and reports BTN_TOOL_DOUBLETAP and BTN_TOUCH. Any other usage returns 0 without doing anything. All the handled usages other than TIPSWITCH (and the unclaimed-input case) fall out of the switch, forward the event to hid->hiddev_hid_event when HID_CLAIMED_HIDDEV is set and that callback exists, and return 1.

Reviewer claims: unclaimed input and pen application return before the tipswitch return (round 1, partly right: unclaimed input returns 1 after hiddev forwarding), unknown usages do nothing and return 0 (right, 844-846); the claim that handled usages return 0 and do not forward to hiddev (round 15) is wrong, they fall to not_claimed_input and return 1 (849-855). name: uclogic_params_ugee_v2_init
prose: Static int (hid-uclogic-params.c:1401-1534) that fills *params for a UGEE v2 tablet interface. It returns -EINVAL if params or hdev is NULL, before anything is read or modified. It reads the driver data and the interface number into local variables, and builds the result in a local struct p. Interface 0 gets a mouse frame from uclogic_params_ugee_v2_init_frame_mouse (its error, if nonzero, is returned); interface 0 and any other interface other than 2 are handled without the pen path (an interface other than 0 and 2 gives an invalid parameter set). For interface 2 it probes the interface with uclogic_probe_interface; if the probe fails it makes p invalid and takes the output path. It then reads a 12-byte string descriptor; if the read does not return exactly 12 it logs with hid_err, makes p invalid and takes the output path. It parses the descriptor with uclogic_params_parse_ugee_v2_desc (a nonzero result is returned), frees the string descriptor, applies the pen report descriptor template (NULL gives -ENOMEM), fills the pen descriptor, id 2 and the first subreport, forces the mouse frame type when UCLOGIC_MOUSE_FRAME_QUIRK is set in the driver quirks, and initialises the frame with the dial initialiser (dial and mouse types) or the buttons initialiser (buttons and any other type); a nonzero result is returned. If the device has a battery it initialises it (an error is logged and returned), then initialises the event hooks (an error is logged and returned). On the output path it copies p into *params, clears the local copy and returns 0, so the invalid-parameter cases above return 0 with *params set to the invalid set. On each error return *params is left unmodified, and the string descriptor and the local parameter set (including the pen report descriptor) are freed.

Reviewer claim that interface 0 is a valid frame-mouse case and not marked invalid is right (1425-1431); the claim that probe and string-descriptor failures are converted to invalid params and return 0 is right (1446-1460). name: uclogic_params_ugee_v2_init
prose: Static int (hid-uclogic-params.c:1401-1534) that fills *params for a UGEE v2 tablet interface. It returns -EINVAL if params or hdev is NULL, before anything is read or modified. It builds the result in a local struct p. Interface 0 gets a mouse-frame parameter set from uclogic_params_ugee_v2_init_frame_mouse (its error, if nonzero, is returned) and goes to the output path. An interface other than 0 and 2 gives an invalid parameter set and goes to the output path. For interface 2 it probes the interface with uclogic_probe_interface; if the probe fails it makes p invalid and takes the output path. It then reads a 12-byte string descriptor; if the read does not return exactly 12 it logs with hid_err, makes p invalid and takes the output path. It parses the descriptor (a nonzero result is returned), frees the string descriptor, applies the pen report descriptor template (NULL gives -ENOMEM), fills the pen descriptor, applies UCLOGIC_MOUSE_FRAME_QUIRK from the driver data, and initialises the frame with the dial initialiser (dial or mouse type) or the buttons initialiser (otherwise), returning a nonzero result. If the device has a battery it initialises it, and it then initialises the event hooks; each failure is logged with hid_err and its result is returned. name: wacom_wac_pen_serial_enforce
prose: Static int (wacom_sys.c:105-172). It returns 0 at once, touching neither the queue nor the serial state, if wacom_wac->serial[0] is already nonzero or the features lack WACOM_QUIRK_TOOLSERIAL. Otherwise it scans every usage of every field of the report whose equivalent usage is HID_DG_INRANGE, HID_DG_TOOLSERIALNUMBER, WACOM_HID_WD_SERIALHI or WACOM_HID_WD_TOOLTYPE, extracting the value from raw_data + 1 and inverting the value for HID_DG_INRANGE (so a zero in-range field counts as nonzero). A usage with a nonzero value sets a flush flag and additionally stores the value into wacom_wac->serial[0] (HID_DG_TOOLSERIALNUMBER, replacing it), ORs it shifted by 32 into serial[0] (WACOM_HID_WD_SERIALHI) or stores it into wacom_wac->id[0] (WACOM_HID_WD_TOOLTYPE); an in-range usage records nothing besides the flag. A usage whose value is 0 sets an insert flag. If flush is set it calls wacom_wac_queue_flush, which replays every queued entry through hid_report_raw_event (an entry whose buffer cannot be allocated is dropped silently, an entry of unexpected size is dropped with a warning, a replay error only logs a warning). Otherwise, if insert is set, it appends raw_data (report_size bytes) to pen_fifo, dropping the oldest entries to make room, and a too-large report is only logged. name: ssi_flush
prose: Static int (omap_ssi_port.c:510-573) that stops all traffic on an HSI port. It takes a runtime PM reference with pm_runtime_get_sync and the port lock with spin_lock_bh, selects the idle pinctrl state, and waits 1 us for racing frames. For each GDD logical channel whose pending message belongs to this port it clears the channel control register, drops one autosuspend runtime PM reference when the message is a read, and clears the channel's message pointer. It then writes zero to the SST buffer and TX state registers and to the SSR RX state, buffer and break registers, reads the SSR error register and writes it back as the error acknowledgement, clears the port's MPU interrupt enable and sets the status bits to 0xffffff00, and clears the GDD MPU interrupt enable and acknowledges all GDD status bits (0xff). For each channel it drops one autosuspend reference if the tx queue is non-empty, then flushes the tx and rx queues with ssi_flush_queue (NULL client, so every message is completed with an error status), and finally flushes the break queue. It selects the default pinctrl state, releases the lock, drops the reference it took at the start and returns 0 (its only return). The function must not be entered with omap_port->lock held, since it takes that lock.

name: hte_ts_dis_en_common
prose: Static int (hte.c:237-305) that enables (en true) or disables (en false) the timestamping of one line. It returns -EINVAL, before taking any lock, if desc is NULL, if desc->hte_data is NULL or if its gdev is NULL. It then takes ei->req_mlock; if the timestamp is not marked HTE_TS_REGISTERED it releases the mutex and returns -EUSERS (not -EINVAL). Otherwise it takes ei->slock with interrupts saved. If the state already matches (enable requested and HTE_TS_DISABLE not set, or disable requested and HTE_TS_DISABLE set) it releases both locks and returns 0 without calling the chip. Otherwise it drops slock, calls the chip's enable or disable op; a nonzero result is logged with dev_warn, req_mlock is released and the result is returned with the flag unchanged. On success it retakes slock, clears HTE_TS_DISABLE (enable) or sets it (disable), releases both locks and returns 0. On each return after the registration test slock (where taken) and req_mlock are released before returning; on the early -EINVAL paths no lock was taken.

name: vmbus_onoffer_rescind
prose: Static void (channel_mgmt.c:1143-1278) that handles a rescind-offer message. It first traces the message and sleeps 1 ms at a time until vmbus_connection.offer_in_progress is zero. Under channel_mutex it looks up the channel for rescind->child_relid; if one is found and its rescind_ref is already set it unlocks and returns; if found and not set it sets rescind_ref and unlocks; if none is found it unlocks, returns, and rescind_ref is not set (the offer failed earlier). For a found channel it records whether it is an hvsock channel or a sub-channel, resets the channel callback, calls vmbus_rescind_cleanup, and sleeps 1 ms at a time until probe_done is set. If the channel has a device_obj and a chn_rescind_callback, it calls the callback, calls check_ready_for_suspend_event when the channel was an hvsock or sub-channel, and returns. If it has a device_obj without that callback, it takes a reference on the device and, if that succeeds, unregisters the vmbus device (outside channel_mutex) and drops the reference. If it has no device_obj but has a primary channel, it takes channel_mutex and calls hv_process_channel_removal when the channel state is CHANNEL_OPEN_STATE, or otherwise completes rescind_event, then releases the mutex. After either of these two branches (and when neither applies) it calls check_ready_for_suspend_event when the channel was an hvsock or sub-channel, without touching the channel again (it may already have been freed).

name: hv_common_cpu_init
prose: Int (hv_common.c:472-546), the CPU online callback for cpu. It picks GFP_ATOMIC when interrupts are disabled, otherwise GFP_KERNEL. If this CPU's hyperv_pcpu_input_arg is still NULL (it is already set when the CPU was online before), it kmallocs one page, or two when hv_output_page_exists(), and returns -ENOMEM if that fails. When there is an output page it stores the second page in hyperv_pcpu_output_arg at that point; in an SNP or TDX guest without a paravisor it then decrypts the memory with set_memory_decrypted, returning its error (the memory is not freed, the output pointer already stored stays set, and the input pointer is not set) or, on success, zeroing it. It publishes the memory in hyperv_pcpu_input_arg only after that. It then reads the VP index MSR, stores it in hv_vp_index[cpu] and raises hv_max_vp_index when it is larger. In a parent partition it kcallocs HV_SYNIC_SINT_COUNT bytes for this CPU's hv_synic_eventring_tail, and when that fails it returns -ENOMEM without undoing the earlier steps (the VP index and input page stay set). Otherwise it returns 0.

name: heartbeat_onchannelcallback
prose: Static void (hv_util.c:510-577), the receive callback of the heartbeat channel (the item name heartbeat_work_func does not exist in this file). It loops reading with vmbus_recvpacket into util_heartbeat.recv_buffer (HV_HYP_PAGE_SIZE bytes). If the read fails it logs a rate-limited error and returns. If the received length is 0 it leaves the loop silently, without logging. If the length is smaller than ICMSG_HDR it logs and leaves the loop. For a negotiate message it calls vmbus_prep_negotiate_resp and logs the negotiated version only when that returns true. For a heartbeat message with a length below ICMSG_HDR plus 8 it logs and leaves the loop without replying; otherwise it increments seq_num. Any other message type sets the status to HV_E_FAIL and logs the type. For negotiate, heartbeat and unknown messages it then sets icflags to TRANSACTION | RESPONSE and sends the buffer back with the same length and request id by vmbus_sendpacket as an in-band packet, ignoring its result, and loops to read the next packet. It returns when a read fails and when the loop is left; nothing is returned.

name: hv_do_map_gpa_hcall
prose: Static int (mshv_root_hv_call.c:184-265) that maps page_struct_count pages (or 2 MB pages) into a guest partition with batched hypercalls. It returns -EINVAL if page_struct_count is 0, if both pages and mmio_spa are nonzero, if HV_MAP_GPA_LARGE_PAGE is set together with a nonzero mmio_spa, or if the large-page flag is set and the count is not a multiple of 512 pages. With the large-page flag the page count is divided by 512 and gfn and indexes are scaled by 2 MB. In each batch it saves and disables local interrupts, fills the page frame list of the per-CPU input page (zero entries when HV_MAP_GPA_NO_ACCESS is set, page_to_pfn of pages[index] when pages is non-NULL, otherwise mmio_spa plus the index), and issues the repeat hypercall HVCALL_MAP_GPA_PAGES with interrupts restored just after it. The batch-fill -EINVAL branch for an out-of-range index would break with interrupts still disabled, but with the 2 MB alignment check it cannot be reached. When the hypercall returns HV_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT_MEMORY it deposits HV_MAP_GPA_DEPOSIT_PAGES pages with hv_call_deposit_pages and returns that error if the deposit fails (retrying otherwise); any other hypercall failure returns the errno translated from the status. The loop advances by the number of reps completed. On an error after at least one rep was completed it unmaps the done pages with hv_call_unmap_gpa_pages (with the large-page flag when set), and returns the error; it returns 0 when every page is mapped.

name: hv_call_delete_vp
prose: Int (mshv_root_hv_call.c:405-417) that asks the hypervisor to delete virtual processor vp_index of partition partition_id. It performs no validation of its arguments itself: it packs the two values into a hv_input_delete_vp, issues the fast hypercall HVCALL_DELETE_VP with it, and returns hv_result_to_errno(status) of the hypercall status. That is 0 when the status is success, the Linux error mapped to the hypervisor status for a known failure status, -EOPNOTSUPP when the status is U64_MAX (hypercalls not possible), and -EIO for an unknown status (hv_common.c:812-825). name: vmbus_bus_init
prose: Static int (vmbus_drv.c:1412-1524) that brings up the VMBus bus. It returns the error of hv_init (after a log message) with nothing else done. It then registers hv_bus (its error is returned, nothing to undo). On a PREEMPT_RT kernel, when vmbus_irq_initialized is false, it registers the per-CPU IRQ kthreads (an error goes to the bus unregister and is returned) and sets vmbus_irq_initialized. If vmbus_irq is -1 it installs vmbus_isr with hv_setup_vmbus_handler; otherwise it allocates vmbus_evt with alloc_percpu (the result is not checked) and requests the per-CPU IRQ, and if that fails it logs, frees vmbus_evt and unwinds to the kthread and bus steps. It then calls hv_synic_alloc, and allocates a per-CPU work_struct (-ENOMEM on failure); each failure there unwinds the synic and interrupt setup. Under cpus_read_lock it schedules vmbus_percpu_work on every online CPU, waits for each, registers the CPU-hotplug online state hyperv/vmbus:online with cpuhp_setup_state_nocalls_cpuslocked, releases the lock and frees the work array; a negative result unwinds as above, otherwise it is stored in hyperv_cpuhp_online. It calls vmbus_connect; if that fails the hotplug state is removed first and the same unwinding follows. On success it registers hyperv_panic_vmbus_unload_block on the panic notifier chain, requests the offers with vmbus_request_offers and returns 0. The unwinding runs, in this order, hv_synic_free, removal of the vmbus handler or freeing of the per-CPU IRQ and vmbus_evt, unregistering the per-CPU kthreads on PREEMPT_RT when they were registered (and clearing vmbus_irq_initialized), and bus_unregister, and returns the failing step's error.

name: vmbus_acpi_add
prose: Static int (vmbus_drv.c:2546-2598, the CONFIG_ACPI version; without CONFIG_ACPI the stub at 2600-2603 ignores its argument and returns 0). It takes the ACPI companion of pdev->dev (there is no NULL check on it) and stores the device in vmbus_root_device. It sets the companion of that device to itself, and when CONFIG_ACPI_CCA_REQUIRED is enabled and no DMA attribute is found it marks the device as coherent (logging that no _CCA was found). It walks the device's _CRS resources with vmbus_walk_resources; if that walk fails it takes the cleanup path, which calls vmbus_mmio_remove and returns -ENODEV. Otherwise it walks up the ancestor devices (stopping at the ACPI root) and walks each one's _CRS; a failing ancestor walk is skipped, and when a successful walk leaves hyperv_mmio set it calls vmbus_reserve_fb and stops the loop. It then returns 0, also when no MMIO range was recorded.

name: abituguru_detect_bank1_sensor_type
prose: Static int (abituguru.c:471-607) that detects whether bank 1 sensor sensor_addr is a voltage sensor, a temperature sensor or not connected; it sleeps (schedule_timeout of 20 ms and 50 ms), so the caller must be able to sleep. If the module parameter bank1_types[sensor_addr] holds a value from ABIT_UGURU_IN_SENSOR to ABIT_UGURU_NC it returns that value without touching the hardware. If reading the sensor fails it returns -ENODEV. If the reading is below 10 or above 250 it logs a warning and returns ABIT_UGURU_NC. Otherwise it writes test settings (a volt alarm with an extreme limit, the low alarm test when the reading is at most 240 and the high alarm test otherwise), waits 20 ms, reads the alarm bank, and if the sensor's alarm bit is set reads the sensor settings back and returns ABIT_UGURU_IN_SENSOR when the expected volt alarm flag is set. If not, it writes a temperature high-alarm test, waits 50 ms and, when the alarm bit is set and the temperature high flag is set in the settings read back, returns ABIT_UGURU_TEMP_SENSOR; otherwise ABIT_UGURU_NC. A failing read or write during the tests leaves the result -ENODEV. Each path after the first test write goes through the restore step, which writes data->bank1_settings[sensor_addr] back, retrying up to 3 times; if all three writes fail it logs an error and returns -ENODEV in place of the result. The early returns before the first test write have nothing to restore.

name: cvt_auto_temp
prose: Static int (adt7462.c:1365-1374) that converts a temperature-zone input to an index. It returns 6 when input is 15 and 5 when input is 9. For any other input it returns -22 (the invalid-argument error) when input is below 1 or is not a power of two, and otherwise the base-2 logarithm of input (0 to 30). It allocates nothing and takes no locks.
contract: /*@ requires \true; ensures (input == 15 ==> result == 6) && (input == 9 ==> result == 5) && ((input != 15 && input != 9 && (input < 1 || (input & (input - 1)) != 0)) ==> result == -22) && ((input != 15 && input != 9 && input >= 1 && (input & (input - 1)) == 0) ==> (0 <= result && result <= 30 && (1 << result) == input)); */

The earlier rejections were a mechanical check on the prose naming the macro for the invalid-argument error and an unbound ilog2 in the old contract; neither concerns the behaviour. The prose no longer uses the macro name and the contract states the power-of-two case without ilog2. R:n/a

name: IN_FROM_REG
prose: Static inline int (dme1737.c:262-265) that converts a voltage register value to millivolts. It returns (reg * nominal + (3 << (res - 3))) / (3 << (res - 2)), that is reg scaled by nominal over 3 * 2^res with rounding to nearest (the added term is half the divisor). res is the register resolution in bits (8 or 16 for the callers), so the shifts are well defined only for res of at least 3 and the products must fit in an int. It has a single return, takes no locks and changes no state.
contract: /*@ requires 3 <= res <= 16 && 0 <= reg <= 65535 && 0 <= nominal <= 20000; ensures result == (reg * nominal + (3 << (res - 3))) / (3 << (res - 2)); */
note: Checked against dme1737.c:262-265. The earlier contract failed random testing with res=86, an out-of-range shift; the precondition now bounds res, reg and nominal so that nothing overflows. R:n/a

name: IN_TO_REG
prose: Static inline int (dme1737.c:267-271) that converts millivolts to the 8-bit limit register value. It first clamps val to the range 0 to 255 * nominal / 192 and then returns DIV_ROUND_CLOSEST(val * 192, nominal), that is the clamped value times 192 divided by nominal with rounding to nearest. For positive nominal the result is in the range 0 to 255. nominal is not checked, so a zero nominal would divide by zero. It has a single return and changes no state.
contract: /*@ requires 1 <= nominal <= 100000; ensures \let m = 255 * nominal / 192; \let v = (val < 0 ? 0 : (val > m ? m : val)); 0 <= result <= 255 && result == (v * 192 + nominal / 2) / nominal; */

name: TEMP_FROM_REG
prose: Static inline int (dme1737.c:279-282) that converts a temperature register value to millidegrees Celsius. It returns (reg * 1000) >> (res - 8), where res is the register resolution in bits (16 for input registers, 8 for limit registers). The shift count must be non-negative and below the width of int, and reg * 1000 must fit in an int; a negative reg is shifted arithmetically on the usual targets. It has a single return and changes no state.
note: Checked against dme1737.c:279-282. The earlier contract failed random testing with res=38, an out-of-range shift; the precondition now bounds res and reg. R:n/a

name: TEMP_TO_REG
prose: Static inline int (dme1737.c:284-288) that converts millidegrees Celsius to an 8-bit limit register value in two's complement. It clamps val to -128000..127000 and returns DIV_ROUND_CLOSEST(val, 1000), that is the clamped value divided by 1000 rounded to nearest with halves away from zero. The result is in the range -128 to 127. It has a single return and changes no state.

name: TEMP_RANGE_FROM_REG
prose: Static inline int (dme1737.c:295-298) that returns the temperature range in millidegrees for a register value. It returns the entry of the TEMP_RANGE table selected by the high nibble of reg, that is TEMP_RANGE[(reg >> 4) & 0x0f] (2000 to 80000). It has a single return and changes no state.

name: TEMP_RANGE_TO_REG
prose: Static int (dme1737.c:300-309) that converts a temperature range in millidegrees to the register value, keeping the low nibble of reg. It looks for the largest index i from 15 down to 1 for which val is above the rounded midpoint (TEMP_RANGE[i] + TEMP_RANGE[i - 1] + 1) / 2, and uses i = 0 when no index qualifies. It returns (reg & 0x0f) | (i << 4), so the low nibble of reg is preserved and the high nibble holds i. It has a single return and changes no state.
contract: /*@ requires \true; ensures 0 <= result <= 255 && (result & 0x0f) == (reg & 0x0f) && \let i = result >> 4; (i == 0 || val > (TEMP_RANGE[i] + TEMP_RANGE[i - 1] + 1) / 2) && (\forall integer k; i < k <= 15 ==> val <= (TEMP_RANGE[k] + TEMP_RANGE[k - 1] + 1) / 2); */

name: TEMP_HYST_FROM_REG
prose: Static inline int (dme1737.c:318-321) that extracts a temperature hysteresis from a register byte in millidegrees. For ix equal to 1 it takes the low nibble of reg, for any other ix the high nibble (reg >> 4), and returns that 4-bit value times 1000. It has a single return and changes no state.
note: Checked against dme1737.c:318-321. The earlier rejection was only the missing requires clause. R:n/a

name: TEMP_HYST_TO_REG
prose: Static inline int (dme1737.c:323-329) that converts a hysteresis to its 4-bit register field. It clamps hyst to the range temp - 15000 to temp, converts the difference temp - hyst to units of 1000 with rounding to nearest (a value in the range 0 to 15), and merges it into reg: for ix equal to 1 it keeps the high nibble of reg and puts the value in the low nibble, otherwise it keeps the low nibble and puts the value in the high nibble. It has a single return and changes no state.
contract: /*@ requires -1000000 <= temp <= 1000000; ensures \let c = (hyst < temp - 15000 ? temp - 15000 : (hyst > temp ? temp : hyst)); \let h = (temp - c + 500) / 1000; result == ((ix == 1) ? ((reg & 0xf0) | h) : ((reg & 0x0f) | (h << 4))); */

name: FAN_FROM_REG
prose: Static inline int (dme1737.c:332-338) that converts a fan tachometer register to RPM. When tpc is nonzero it returns tpc * reg. When tpc is 0 it returns 0 for a reg of 0 or 0xffff and otherwise 90000 * 60 / reg (5400000 / reg). It has a single return per branch and changes no state.

name: FAN_TO_REG
prose: Static inline int (dme1737.c:340-348) that converts RPM to a fan tachometer register. When tpc is nonzero it returns val / tpc clamped to 0..0xffff. When tpc is 0 it returns 0xffff for val at or below 0, and otherwise 90000 * 60 / val (5400000 / val) clamped to 0..0xfffe. A nonzero tpc is expected to be positive; the callers pass 0 or a divisor from FAN_TPC_FROM_REG. It has a single return per branch and changes no state.
